name: Pan-Arabism
summary: Pan-Arabism holds that the Arabs form one nation from the Atlantic to the Arabian Sea, with a natural right to a single state, and seeks union of the Arab states against colonial partition and Western influence. In its mainstream Ba'thist and Nasserist forms it is secular-leaning, socialist in a national rather than class sense, hostile to Zionism, and non-aligned, with state control of key industries and a record of strong-executive rule.
scope: The mid-20th-century mainstream: Ba'thism (Aflaq, al-Bitar, al-Arsuzi, 1947 constitution) and Nasserism, with al-Husri's language-based definition of the nation. It excludes pan-Islamism, Syrian-nationalist (Greater Syria) and local-state nationalisms, and the later Saddam-era and Assad-era regimes' practice except where noted.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Ba'th program promised free public health care and education for all, funded by the state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The constitution seeks fairer distribution of wealth and worker protection, but sets no wage floor; inferred from its socialist aims.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ba'th and Nasserist socialism put key industries, trade and banking under state control and distrusted unregulated markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The 1947 constitution places key industries, resources and transport under state ownership and abolishes foreign concessions.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The program calls for fairer wealth distribution and capped holdings, implying heavier burdens on the rich, though taxes are not spelled out.

unions-good.rationale: The constitution has workers share in management and profits and the party courted trade unions, though Arab socialist states later controlled unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is a natural right only within national-interest limits, with caps on holdings and bans on exploitative use.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Foreign companies are abolished, the state controls trade, and large undertakings are nationalized, a stronger step than regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: The program promised state-provided health, education and guaranteed employment; cutting welfare opposes it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers were to share in wages and management, but the program stops at state ownership and capped private property rather than worker ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Arab nationalist regimes built security states with little interest in civil liberties; the founding texts do not address surveillance, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist movements stressing community moral character and conservative values would likely oppose legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution limits press freedom by national interest, but adherents are not documented as split either way on hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Pan-Arabism gravitated to Nasser's charismatic leadership, and Aflaq backed a strong single executive to achieve unity.

state-harmful.rationale: Pan-Arabism seeks a strong Arab state; the nation's natural right is to live in a single state.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is silent, and it favoured compulsory military service rather than civilian arms policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nationalist movements prized strong armies, compulsory service and military role in politics, though the Ba'th long decried military intrusion.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; the movement framed women as bearers of the nation in conservative terms, so inferred opposition.

decide-locally.rationale: Pan-Arabism wants a unified Arab state, and Nasser's UAR was a unitary state centralizing power against local structures.

rehabilitation.rationale: The movement did not address penal philosophy; no basis for a stance.

traditional-family.rationale: Nationalist discourse cast women as bearers of the nation in conservative terms, though the Ba'th also promoted women's equality; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; conservative social outlook of mainstream Arab nationalism implies opposition, so low confidence.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from socially conservative outlook and pronatalist national-strength thinking.

more-religion-public.rationale: Pan-Arabism began as secular and rivalled pan-Islamism, though Aflaq saw Islam as expressing Arab genius, so it prefers a limited public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern in the texts; Arabization policies suggest indifference or hostility to minority redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; movement favoured women's civic equality but in a conservative gender framing.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Arab nationalism defines the nation by language, culture and history and treats their revival as central.

gradual-change.rationale: The Ba'th called itself revolutionary, and Aflaq's inqilab envisioned structural transformation rather than gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalism is open to Arabic speakers across borders, while states restricted others.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The program condemns foreign influence and values sovereignty; Arab League cooperation is favoured, but Western-led bodies are distrusted.

free-trade.rationale: The state controls foreign and domestic trade under the Ba'th constitution, and Arab socialism favoured protection and economic independence.

nation-first.rationale: The program ranks Arab national interests and sovereignty first, though it also describes cooperation in a peaceful world.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Arab nationalism is rooted in anti-colonialism and viewed Western intervention as imperialism.

open-borders.rationale: Within the Arab world, borders were seen as colonial and meant to dissolve; beyond it no open-border aim exists.

limit-growth.rationale: Arab socialism pursued industrialization and development; limiting growth is not in its outlook.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed in the movement's founding era; no basis for a stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; the movement valued modernization but made no claim on technology solving problems.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalist states pursued development but no doctrine on nuclear power exists.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Ba'th declared itself revolutionary and its Aflaq sought inqilab; Arab nationalists backed coups and revolutions against mandates and monarchies.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's military and party vanguards ruled on behalf of the people, but this is not framed as expertise.

central-planning.rationale: Arab socialism put the state in control of major undertakings and trade, though the Ba'th rejected Marxist economic determinism and kept limited private property.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the program keeps limited private enterprise alongside state ownership and worker profit-sharing, so adherents could go either way.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian reform and capped landholdings were the land policy instead.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance is a natural right in the constitution but limited by the national interest and caps on holdings.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the program favoured guaranteed employment rather than cash transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: State control of foreign trade and abolition of foreign concessions imply protection for domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The constitution gives the state control over major industry, trade and the bank, which implies directing investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The constitution caps agricultural and industrial holdings and allows small property but also state ownership; no clear position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The program preserves wages, banks and limited private property; Aflaq rejected Marxist class abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The constitution creates a single state bank and wants state control of finance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; workers' participation in management exists, but state-recognized bargaining bodies are not described.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ba'th and Nasserist states became single-party regimes, and Nasser demanded a single party in the UAR, though the 1947 text calls for representative government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Arab nationalists overthrew or opposed monarchies as British-backed, as in Egypt in 1952 and Iraq in 1958.

democracy-best.rationale: The Ba'th espoused parliamentary democracy in its programme but sacrificed it once in power, so adherents are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; plebiscites were used by Arab nationalist regimes but referenda are not a principle.

workers-councils.rationale: The Ba'th rejected class-based rule; it wanted national representative government rather than workers' councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Pan-Arabism seeks to unify the Arab nation, and Ba'thist states suppressed Kurdish autonomy claims.

natural-rulers.rationale: The program stresses equality of citizens and opposes tribal and sectarian privilege, though vanguard party rule implies guidance.

political-violence-never.rationale: Arab nationalists fought the mandates and Israel and used coups and violence; the movement rejects pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Romantic nationalism glorified struggle for resurrection, but no explicit doctrine on war building character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Pan-Arabism began as a secular movement and the Ba'th was opposed by the Muslim Brotherhood for its secularism, though Aflaq honoured Islam culturally.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Mainstream pan-Arabism put nation above religion and rivalled Islamist movements; the 1947 constitution has no sharia clause.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Ba'th state controls key services and military service is compulsory; privatizing defence is foreign to it.

military-superiority.rationale: Arab nationalists sought strong armies to liberate Palestine and resist the West, but superiority over rivals is not stated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Arab nation is defined by language and shared belonging rather than blood, so it is cultural-ethnic, and Arabization displaced Kurds.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Ba'th rejects economic determinism and sees socialism arising from a majority of society, not one class; nationalism is the driving force.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The program seeks fairer wealth distribution and caps holdings but also keeps private property, so outcomes equality is not stated.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalists claimed Arab land against Israel but do not articulate this rights doctrine.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Ba'th condemned colonialism as a crime and wanted treaties infringing sovereignty annulled, implying support for redress.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Arabism holds that Arabs form one nation and should unite in one state from the Atlantic to the Arabian Sea.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The movement is collectivist, treating socialism as a means to national resurrection.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The constitution stresses national bonds overriding sectarian ones and sets freedoms within national interest limits.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; strength through numbers is plausibly valued but not stated.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Arab socialism pursued state-led industrialization as part of resurgence.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed; modernization was valued but disruption of institutions was not an aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed in the founding era.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; security-state regimes would oppose citizens' uncrackable encryption, so inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pan-Arabism invokes a past golden age for resurrection yet aims at modern revolutionary change, so it rejects mere restoration over progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Ba'th was a strongly ideological party, though criticised for lacking realism.

direct-action.rationale: Adherents used both elections and coups and street demonstrations; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Aflaq criticised violence as distrust of the people, but Ba'thist parties also used coups; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement sought development and modernization, not primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of the Ba'th programme, which accepts wages and organized industry.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The program seeks fairer distribution but within wages and property, not need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: State ownership of major industry aims at social benefit over private profit, but is not framed in these terms.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Property is limited by its exploitative effect, but Aflaq rejected Marxist class analysis, so the claim is not adopted wholesale.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Ba'th opposed communism and rejected class-based rule in favour of national socialism.

collective-farming.rationale: The program caps holdings and favours agrarian reform to small farmers, not collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialism blamed Western powers for domination, but Aflaq rejected Marxist theory of capitalism; unstated.

taxation-theft.rationale: Statist programme with state-provided services; taxation is unobjectionable.

harm-principle.rationale: Freedoms are bounded by national interest in the constitution, wider than the harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Ba'th stressed the nation's right to a state and national bonds over individual claims.

conscription.rationale: The 1947 constitution makes military service compulsory.

exit-over-voice.rationale: A statist, national-unity movement opposes exit as a check.

state-as-business.rationale: The movement sees the state as a socialist, national agent, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Ba'th paired freedom with socialism and guaranteed jobs, health and education to make freedom real.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The constitution rejects racial divisions and defines Arab identity by language and loyalty, not genes.

organic-representation.rationale: The constitution envisions a constitutional representative system; corporatist organic representation is not stated.

total-state.rationale: Nasser's and Ba'thist regimes controlled the economy, media and education, but the founding text guarantees freedoms; split.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ba'th means renaissance or resurrection, and its mission is to revive the Arab nation after decline.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Unification of the Arab world is expansion beyond one state, but is framed as unity, not conquest; Iraq and Syria diverged.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The program is modern, socialist and representative; feudal oaths are foreign.

bound-labor.rationale: The program calls for agrarian reform and capped holdings against feudal landlords.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Aflaq's romantic nationalism stresses the nation's distinct spirit.

single-common-good.rationale: Ba'th socialism rests on the conviction of the whole society rather than one class, implying a common national interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Opposition to Zionism and Israel is a central rallying point of Arab nationalism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed directly; Arab nationalists backed the Palestinian return, while opposing Jewish return to Israel, so adherents would oppose the general rule as applied by Israel; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: Arabic is the official language of the Arab state in the constitution, and language defines the nation, but Arabic never fell out of use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The constitution gives workers a share in management and profits of large undertakings.

school-vouchers.rationale: The constitution abolishes private and foreign schools and makes education a state responsibility.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: State-led development was financed actively by the state; austerity is foreign to it.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement ranks national unity and state economic control above economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Ba'th constitution states the Arab nation has a natural right to its own state.

force-without-un.rationale: Nationalists saw the UN as Western-influenced and backed armed struggle against Israel and colonial powers; not explicitly stated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Aflaq's romantic nationalism stressed spirit and emotion over rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The constitution speaks of citizens' benefits; migrant policy not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; guaranteed employment was a state duty.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Ba'th saw socialism as national, arising from the whole society, and rejected class warfare, while keeping workers' participation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement treats heritage, language and history as the basis of nationhood.

dominated-front.rationale: Pan-Arabism seeks to strengthen Arab states against Western powers and the Ba'th favoured non-alignment and anti-imperial cooperation.

workers-nation.rationale: The Ba'th regarded Western socialism as imperialism and put national socialism above international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Ba'th called for equality of sexes and women's vote, though nationalism cast women as bearers of the nation.

ban-interest.rationale: The 1947 constitution outlaws usury and creates a single state bank.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution sets national bonds above racial division.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Ba'th rejected the Marxist class reading of the state and saw it as a national agent.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Arab oil was seen as national wealth under state control; expansion is inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Arab identity is defined by language and loyalty, so Arabization was pursued, as against Kurds; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not part of pan-Arabism, and not documented.

proportional-representation.rationale: The constitution wants representative government without specifying an electoral system.

national-mission.rationale: Aflaq spoke of an eternal mission for the Arab nation and the Ba'th sought to inspire resurrection beyond Syria.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Ba'th supported equal rights for women but did not frame society as structurally patriarchal.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Arab nationalists denounced landed elites and rich merchants and the old notable-led governments.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed and out of line with the movement's welfare orientation.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Regimes born of the movement used security forces against opponents; accountability not a principle.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The program gives the state wide economic and social roles.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The Ba'th defines identity by language and attachment, opposing racial divisions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution affirms civic equality including women, though minority provisions are thin.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Arab socialism is nationalist, seeking socialism within an Arab state, not world revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Arab nationalists viewed Israel as an imperialist colonial implant; the proposition is consistent with that view.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; Arab regimes left personal status laws sectarian.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No such tradition in Arab nationalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The state controls education, but Aflaq honoured Islam; religious instruction was retained in Arab state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a Ba'th doctrine; the party stressed a strong state for the Arab nation.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The program promises representative government but regimes ruled without free consent; split.

trade-surplus.rationale: State trade control exists but no export surplus aim is stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Arab nationalism opposed Israel's displacement of Palestinians, yet Ba'thist states displaced Kurds; split, inferred opposition.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Movement embraced armed struggle and coups.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement stressed national solidarity rather than struggle between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Arab nationalist governments routinely banned parties, including communists and Islamists.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not addressed, though freedom from foreign domination is central.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitution calls for an executive answerable to the people, but states concentrated power; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Ba'th was a cadre party that sought influence in the army, but Aflaq rejected the Leninist class vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Ba'th promised free health and education and jobs and backed agrarian reform against landed elites.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The constitution allows real estate property without exploitation; not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Workers' participation but later state control of unions; split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The movement blamed colonialism and feudal elites for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Arab nationalists prized cohesion but divided over minorities; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The constitution calls for representative government with elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Arab nationalist regimes ruled under emergency law, as in Syria.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State control of trade and economic planning supports price controls.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nasser banned autonomous organizations and Ba'thist states controlled media, though the 1947 text limited press freedom only by national interest.

party-commands-army.rationale: Ba'th cadres worked inside the army and later stood over it, but the party originally decried military involvement.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Ba'th was a disciplined cadre party with a National Command, so binding party decisions are consistent.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Pan-Arabism seeks union of Arab states into one, as the UAR.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nasser's UAR had a single executive commanding the forces, and Ba'th insisted on executive authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; no relevance. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

clerical-rule.rationale: Secular pan-Arabism rivals Islamist politics and was opposed by clerical movements.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement is nationalist and put national loyalty above international class.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed, though freedom of art is sacred in the constitution; regimes censored.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nasser was returned in landslide votes and no term limits applied; candidate, inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The Ba'th preferred non-alignment out of the belief that neither bloc cared for Arab interests.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The constitution allows real estate property so long as it is not exploitative; no ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: The constitution uses compulsory service in a national army, not a militia.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed. Inferred from its general principles, so low confidence.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Arabism regards the Sykes-Picot borders as imposed, and seeks restoring the divided Arab nation.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Ba'th was built by intellectuals and students.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Arab nationalism emphasizes the Arab nation's special mission and cultural pride.

death-penalty.rationale: Arab nationalist regimes used capital punishment, as for Qasim; not doctrine.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Gender equality was espoused, sex education not addressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Secular Ba'th education favours modern curricula, but religion in schools is kept; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Socially conservative nationalist movements restricted it; not doctrine.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Arab identity is defined by language and belonging, and Arab descent underlay the pan-Arab nation.

minority-language-support.rationale: Arabic is official language and Arabization displaced Kurds.

religious-exemptions.rationale: National bonds override sectarian divisions in the constitution.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nationalist collectivism does not encourage nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialism led to nationalizing foreign holdings and cancelling concessions.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Aflaq saw socialism as the means of national resurrection, and the Ba'th abolished foreign concessions.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; adherents seized power by coups.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Arab nationalist regimes limited political freedom for development and unity, though the Ba'th originally prized freedom.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The constitution describes a peaceful cooperative world; aid duty is inferred from anti-colonialism.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; Arab nationalists sought strength against Israel and the West, inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nasser was confirmed by plebiscite with 99 percent, and a single executive was preferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The constitution creates one state bank under state control.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Arab nationalists rejected recognition of Israel and saw Palestine as Arab land, though later regimes negotiated; majority view.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution makes property and inheritance rights subject to national-interest and anti-exploitation limits.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ba'thists labelled Nasser's nationalizations state capitalism but kept relations with the USSR; unaddressed for the Soviet Union itself.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Mid-century Ba'thism and Nasserism prioritised state-led industrialisation and never addressed environmental precaution, so there is no inferable lean.

collective-defense.rationale: Arab unity implies that an attack on one Arab state is an attack on the whole nation, as in the Arab League's joint defence arrangements.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Arab nationalists treat Israeli control of Palestine and the Golan, and French annexation of Alexandretta, as illegitimate occupation of Arab land however long it lasts.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the secular-leaning, state-centred character of Ba'thism and Nasserism, which put religious institutions under state control; not stated in the sources used.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from practice: Nasserist and Ba'thist presidents led the single ruling party and the movement rather than standing above politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the commitment to a single Arab state and the strong-executive record, which treated separatism as a threat to national unity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The programme calls for one unified Arab state with a single system; some federal unions were accepted tactically, but the mainstream aim is uniformity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Mainstream pan-Arabism is secular-leaning and republican, and it fought the Arab monarchies as reactionary.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Ba'thist and Nasserist socialism favours state redistribution and progressive taxation, not a uniform rate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on education and social transformation to forge a new Arab generation.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Doctrine holds constitutional government, though regimes in practice ruled by emergency powers; inferred and contested.

space-expansion.rationale: The mid-century movement never addressed space; adherents are indifferent, with no principle pointing either way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from preference for a single national party and strong executive over a balance of social orders.

leader-cult.rationale: Nasser's cult of personality, with portraits and mass rallies, was a feature of the movement, though the doctrine itself does not demand it.

equal-parenting.rationale: The movement backed women's civic equality but never addressed custody after separation; adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Aflaq's national socialism rejects Marxist class struggle and is anti-communist.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the socialist program and the Ba'thist and Nasserist land reforms; not stated in the cited excerpt.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to Zionism and the central place of Palestine; not stated in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Arabism holds the Arabs are one nation with a right to one state, so Arab-inhabited land beyond borders is part of it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the secular-leaning mainstream, which did not enforce religious law; not addressed in the sources.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the secular-leaning mainstream and the 1947 call for women's equality.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from the goal of Arab union, as in the Nasser-era United Arab Republic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Arabism's defining goal is political union of kindred Arab peoples across colonial borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from the language-based single nation, which leaves little room for separate minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to Zionist homeland-building as a response to persecution; not stated directly.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Aflaq's national socialism is idealist and rejects Marxist historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The state-ownership program does not address cartels directly; adherents' view is unclear.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred from state control of key industries; failing firms were nationalized or supported, not left to fail.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from the strong-executive practice of Ba'thist and Nasserist states, where courts were subordinate.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The 1947 constitution promises equality of the sexes but not quotas; adherents are unclear.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from the push for Arab economic integration and independence from Western economic influence.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' view is unclear.

moral-incentives.rationale: Aflaq's national socialism rests on national duty and state welfare rather than Guevarist moral incentives; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from the Ba'thist and Nasserist record of coups and revolution led by party and officer cells.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the movement's republican, anti-monarchical record; not stated in the sources.

missingStatements.text: Foreign companies and concessions should be abolished and their holdings taken into national ownership.
missingStatements.rationale: The Ba'th constitution abolishes foreign concessions and companies as a core anti-imperial economic measure.

missingStatements.text: Compulsory free public education should be provided only by the state, with private schools abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1947 constitution makes education a state responsibility and abolishes private and foreign schools.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic to the Ba'th constitution; secondary to the broader economic-independence position.

missingStatements.text: Women should have the same civic and voting rights as men.
missingStatements.rationale: The Ba'th called for equality of the sexes and women's vote from its first convention.

notes: Strands differ: Nasserism was more authoritarian and state-capitalist, Ba'thism more doctrinal; the Iraqi and Syrian Ba'th diverged. Islamic reference grew later in the movement. Only s2 supports several statements on which pan-Arabism did not speak directly, so many answers are low confidence.
